implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 was adopted in 2024 and revised and approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). Procedures exist for workforce accounts; procedures for network element and vendor access are being written under STD-06.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); BSS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Workforce accounts are provisioned in the identity provider from the HR system and federated to the BSS, OSS, cloud accounts, and CCaaS. Terminations disable IdP access automatically. Gaps: access reviews are semiannual, not quarterly; network element local accounts and SYS-18 accounts are outside the lifecycle; P07 found 5 of 25 sampled transfers kept prior BSS roles.
evidence: HR feed configuration; IdP export; access review record February 2026; P07 samples

implementation_statement: Account creation, disablement, and removal for federated applications is automated through the HR-driven identity provider workflow.
IdP accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically. Local accounts on network elements, jump hosts, and SYS-18 are not covered.
evidence: IdP inactivity policy; P07 AC-2 results

implementation_statement: IdP and cloud account changes are logged and sent to the SIEM, where the MDR alerts on new administrator grants. TACACS+ and SYS-18 account changes are not logged centrally.
evidence: SIEM rule list; MDR alert samples

provider_if_inherited: BSS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Role-based access is enforced in the BSS (32 roles), OSS, cloud accounts (permission sets mapped to directory groups), and CCaaS. CPNI screens in the BSS show the approval flag and require the customer authentication step before call detail is displayed.
evidence: BSS role catalog; permission set export

implementation_statement: Information flows between the corporate network, the management network, and the cloud are enforced by firewalls at CO-1 and CO-4 and by the cloud network hub. Gap: at POP-A and POP-B the management VLAN is routable from corporate VLANs (gap 5).
evidence: Firewall rule exports; P07 SC-7 reachability test

implementation_statement: Duties are separated for billing adjustments (requester and approver) and for cloud administration versus backup administration. Network engineers can both change and approve element configurations outside the core.
evidence: BSS adjustment workflow; backup account administrator list

implementation_statement: Least privilege is applied in the BSS and cloud. Gaps: shared local administrator accounts on access elements and SBCs give every network engineer full rights; 61 BSS users hold the bulk export right, which only 9 roles need (P07).
evidence: BSS export rights report; P07 AC-6 results

implementation_statement: Access to security functions (SIEM, EDR console, IdP administration) is limited to the security team and 3 IT administrators. TACACS+ policy changes can be made by any network engineer.
IT administrators use separate administrator accounts for servers and cloud. Network engineers use the same shared local accounts for administration of access elements.
Privileged access management with vaulting and session recording covers Windows servers and cloud accounts. It does not cover network elements, SYS-18, or the hosted voice cluster.
Privileged functions in cloud and on servers are logged to the SIEM. TACACS+ command accounting is kept 90 days on the TACACS+ servers and not reviewed.
evidence: SIEM sources list; TACACS+ log retention

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts after 10 failed attempts and applies risk-based sign-in checks. The BSS and portal lock after 5 failed customer password attempts.
Network elements, jump hosts, and servers display an authorized-use banner before login.
Workstations lock after 10 minutes idle through device management policy.

provider_if_inherited: BSS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: BSS agent sessions end after 30 minutes idle; IdP sessions require re-authentication every 12 hours.

Remote access uses the VPN with IdP MFA and device posture checks. Vendor remote access to OLTs and SBCs uses a shared VPN account with standing access to the management network (found in P07; POAM-003).
evidence: VPN configuration; vendor access list; P07 AC-17 and MA-4 results

implementation_statement: VPN sessions are logged and sent to the SIEM; vendor sessions are not recorded.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote access sessions use TLS or IPsec with approved ciphers (STD-08).
Corporate Wi-Fi uses certificate-based authentication; guest Wi-Fi is isolated from corporate and management networks.
Field tablets are enrolled in mobile device management with encryption, a passcode, and remote wipe.
Use of external systems is governed by POL-05; staff may not use personal devices for CPNI. Public generative AI tools are used by staff without approval (P10 AI-005).
Awareness and training policy is part of POL-05, approved 2026-09-17.
All employees complete security awareness and CPNI training at hire and annually; phishing simulations run quarterly (June 2026 click rate 6.1%).
Training covers pretexting and insider misuse of CPNI. There is no specific insider threat module for network engineers with privileged access.

Role-based CPNI training exists for in-house care and retail staff. Gaps: overflow call center vendor agents and chatbot vendor staff have not been trained; network engineers have no role-based security training (P07 AT-3).
Logging requirements are stated in POL-03; the logging standard STD-02 is in draft (due 2027-01-31).

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2); BSS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Logged events are defined for IdP, cloud, EDR, firewalls, VPN, and BSS audit logs. Gaps: network element syslog and TACACS+ accounting, CDR archive object reads, SYS-15, and SYS-18 are not defined or collected (gap 7).
evidence: SIEM sources list; P07 AU-2 results

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2); Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Audit records from cloud and IdP sources contain time, source, user, event type, and outcome.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MDR reviews SIEM alerts 24x7. Gaps: BSS call detail views are not reviewed for inappropriate access; no one reviews TACACS+ accounting.
evidence: MDR monthly reports; P07 AU-6 results

implementation_statement: Automated correlation of BSS access logs with care tickets is planned with the logging standard (2027-03-31).
Network elements, servers, and cloud services synchronize to company NTP servers fed by GPS clocks at CO-1 and CO-4.
Cloud and SIEM logs are copied to the write-once log archive in the security account; only the security team can read it.
SIEM retains 1 year searchable and the log archive 3 years. Network element syslog is kept 90 days locally, which is too short for intrusion investigations.

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2); BSS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Audit record generation is enabled by default in the cloud, IdP, and BSS services.
Controls are assessed annually by the co-sourced internal audit firm, which does not operate them (P07, 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-21).

Interconnections with the TTP, SS7 hub, NG911 provider, and BSS vendor are covered by contracts. Interconnection terms for the chatbot and CCaaS API integrations do not address CPNI handling or incident notice.
The POA&M (P07 poam.csv) tracks every weakness with an owner and date and is reviewed quarterly by the COO and the audit committee.
The COO accepted operation of the OSS/BSS with conditions on 2026-09-17; the CEO accepted the High risks with dated treatment plans (SSP section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring covers vulnerability scans of servers and cloud, MDR alerting, and cloud posture checks. Network elements are not in the monitoring strategy.
Configuration management requirements are in POL-01; the configuration standard STD-01 is in draft (due 2027-03-31).
Golden configurations exist for core routers and broadband network gateways. There are no documented baselines for OLTs, DSLAMs, cabinet switches, SBCs, or cloud virtual machines.
evidence: Golden configuration repository; P07 CM-2 results

implementation_statement: Network changes go through the change advisory board with maintenance windows. Hosted voice platform changes and cloud infrastructure changes are not consistently ticketed (P07 CM-3: 7 of 25 sampled changes had no approval record).
Impact analysis is required for network changes in maintenance windows, including 911 circuit impact. Cloud and Business Services changes have no documented impact analysis.
Cloud organization guardrails enforce encryption and block public storage; servers follow vendor benchmarks informally. P07 found default SNMP community strings on 9 of 25 sampled cabinet switches.
Unneeded services are disabled on core routers. Telnet and HTTP management remain enabled on some access elements.
Inventories exist in the OSS (network elements) and the endpoint manager (endpoints). The OSS inventory does not include about 140 CLEC metro devices at POP-A and POP-B or their software versions.
evidence: OSS inventory export; P07 CM-8 results

implementation_statement: Automatic inventory updates on install and removal will come with the OSS discovery module (2027-03-31).
Users cannot install software on managed endpoints; installs go through the software catalog.
Contingency requirements are in POL-03 and POL-04; the contingency and recovery standard STD-07 is in draft (due 2026-12-31).

The NOC storm and outage plan covers network service, PSAP notice, and DIRS. There is no IT contingency plan for the cloud workloads, the BSS outage, or SYS-18 (gap 9). Recovery objectives now come from the BIA (P05).
evidence: NOC outage plan; P05 BIA; P07 CP-2 results

implementation_statement: The NOC plan is coordinated with the state NG911 provider and PSAPs. IT recovery is not coordinated with the BSS and CCaaS vendors.
Resumption of High-criticality processes within their RTOs is demonstrated for voice and broadband (storm events) but not for cloud-hosted processes.
NOC staff train on outage and storm procedures each spring. IT staff have no contingency training.
Restore testing is done for the OSS (2026-04). Mediation, portal, data warehouse, hosted voice configuration, and network element bulk restores are untested.
evidence: Restore test record 2026-04; P07 CP-4 results

implementation_statement: Cloud backups are stored in the backup account in a second region; network element configurations are copied to CO-4.
The backup region is geographically separated from the production region; CO-4 is about 40 miles from CO-1.
Alternate processing exists for the NOC (CO-4) and voice core (CO-4 node). Cloud workloads would be rebuilt in the second region, but no runbook exists.
CO-1 and CO-4 each have two diverse transit providers and diverse fiber entrances.
Daily backups of the production account to the backup account with 35-day write-once retention and separate administrator credentials; nightly network element configuration backups.
evidence: Backup job reports (30 of 30 days in July 2026)

implementation_statement: Backup integrity is checked by the backup service; restores are tested only for the OSS.
Recovery procedures exist for network elements (re-apply configuration). Cloud workload recovery and reconstitution procedures are not written.
Identification and authentication policy is part of POL-02, approved 2026-09-17.
Workforce users have unique IdP accounts. Shared local administrator accounts on access elements, SBCs, and SYS-18 are not uniquely identified (gap 5).
MFA is enforced for privileged IdP, cloud, and server accounts, and through TACACS+ for core and edge routers. Privileged access to access elements, SBCs, and SYS-18 has no MFA.
MFA is enforced for all non-privileged workforce access to federated applications and the VPN.
Push MFA with number matching is replay resistant; hardware security keys are used by cloud and identity administrators. SMS codes remain as a fallback for 40 field supervisors.
Broadband customer devices are authenticated by the broadband network gateways; network elements authenticate to TACACS+ with shared keys that have not been rotated since 2022.
Identifiers are assigned from the HR record and never reused.

IdP passwords follow a 14-character minimum and banned list. Gaps: shared network element passwords are not rotated when engineers leave; default SNMP strings were found on cabinet switches; service account secrets for mediation are stored in a configuration file.

Customer (non-organizational user) authentication for online CPNI access uses a password set after a one-time code to the telephone number or email of record (64.2010(c), (e)). Gap: the chatbot "verify me" fallback accepts SSN4 plus service address (gap 1); SYS-18 business portal uses account number and ZIP for password reset.
evidence: Portal configuration; chatbot test 2026-07-22; P07 IA-8 result

implementation_statement: Incident response policy POL-03 approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01.
Security team and MDR are trained; NOC, regulatory affairs, and customer operations have not been trained on the CPNI and outage notification steps.
One IT-only tabletop was held in 2025. The P08 runbooks will be exercised with the NOC, regulatory affairs, and counsel on 2026-11-19.
The MDR triages and contains endpoint and cloud incidents 24x7. Incident handling for network element intrusions and CPNI breach determination was not defined until the P08 runbooks (2026-09-17).
evidence: MDR runbooks; incident log; P07 IR-4 results

implementation_statement: Incidents are logged in the ticketing system under the Security category, which also serves as the CPNI breach record (64.2011(d)).
Outage reporting to PSAPs and NORS works (6 NORS filings in 12 months). The CPNI breach procedure in the 2024 plan used the wrong (not yet effective) rule text; the corrected matrix is in P08.
evidence: NORS filing records; P08 notification matrix

implementation_statement: The MDR provider and the insurer panel provide incident response assistance and forensics.
The 2024 incident response plan is replaced by the two P08 runbooks and the notification matrix, approved 2026-09-17; not yet exercised.
Network element maintenance is scheduled in maintenance windows with change tickets and vendor return authorizations.
Nonlocal maintenance by OLT and SBC vendors uses a shared VPN account with standing access; sessions are not approved per session or recorded (found in P07).
evidence: Vendor access list; P07 MA-4 results

implementation_statement: Media and network element storage are wiped or destroyed by a certified vendor with certificates of destruction.
Physical access to central offices, POPs, and the data hall is authorized by the facility owner and reviewed quarterly.

Badge access, cameras, and alarms protect central offices, POPs, and the data hall; the CALEA room requires two-person entry. Gaps: POP-B uses keys rather than badges; 3 cabinets in the 4 visited had broken alarm contacts.
Door alarms and camera alerts at central offices route to the NOC 24x7.
Central offices have generators with 72 hours of fuel and about 8 hours of battery. The CO-6 generator failed its full-load test on 2026-05-14 (gap 11).
Central offices and the data hall have fire detection and clean-agent suppression, inspected annually.
Temperature and humidity are monitored in central offices and the data hall, with alarms to the NOC.
This SSP documents the OSS/BSS and is reviewed annually and after major changes.
Rules of behavior (POL-05) are acknowledged at hire and annually by employees; overflow vendor agents acknowledge them through the vendor.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The program is documented in POL-01, the standards index, and this SSP. A program plan with funded roadmap was approved on 2026-09-17; standards are still in draft.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The vCISO leads strategy and board reporting; the Security Manager runs operations; designations are in POL-01 4.2.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The risk management strategy, acceptance authorities, and risk appetite statements are in P01 and POL-01 4.4, approved by the CEO on 2026-09-17.
Background checks are completed before hire for all employees; CALEA-authorized employees get an enhanced check.
IdP access is disabled on the termination date. Gaps: shared network element passwords are not rotated at departure; 2 of 25 sampled terminated users kept SYS-18 accounts (P07 PS-4).
Transfers trigger a manager review of access, but prior roles are not removed automatically (5 of 25 sampled kept prior BSS roles).
The overflow call center contract requires confidentiality but not CPNI training, background checks, or 24-hour incident notice.
The sanctions procedure (POL-01 4.8) expressly covers CPNI misuse; 3 CPNI-related sanctions were recorded in 2025-2026.

control_name: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information
baseline: Privacy baseline (selected because the platform processes CPNI)
implementation_statement: Authority to process CPNI is documented in the CPNI operating procedures (64.2005). The churn model (AI-004) uses CPNI without a documented authority or approval check.

baseline: Privacy baseline (selected because the platform processes CPNI)
implementation_statement: Opt-out approval is recorded on every BSS account and shown to agents. The campaign tool and the churn model do not check the flag before using CPNI (64.2009(a)).
evidence: BSS approval flag report; campaign register

baseline: Privacy baseline (selected because the platform processes CPNI)
implementation_statement: CPNI notices are mailed before solicitation; the biennial opt-out notice was sent in 2025. The Spanish notice translates only part of the English text (64.2008(c)(8)).
The OSS/BSS is categorized Moderate (SSP section 6).
Enterprise and system risk assessments use NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01, 2026-07-31; updated 2026-08-14).
Supply chain risk is assessed for 12 Tier 1 vendors; 22 of 34 vendors with CPNI, PII, or network access are unreviewed.
Monthly authenticated scans cover servers and cloud; quarterly external scans cover internet-facing addresses. Network elements are not scanned (gap 6).
Scanner vulnerability feeds update daily.
Risk responses are recorded in the risk register and POA&M with owners and dates.
Critical components are identified from the BIA (P05): voice core, 911 facilities, management plane, BSS.

Contracts for network equipment include security patch support terms. SaaS contracts for the chatbot and agent assist lack CPNI, no-training, and incident notice terms. Purchasing does not check the FCC Covered List for used equipment.
Security architecture principles (segmentation of the management plane, least privilege) are stated in POL-01 but not yet applied at the POPs.

provider_if_inherited: BSS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2); Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: External services are inventoried. The 12 Tier 1 vendors were reviewed in 2026 (SOC 2 reports or, where none exists, questionnaires; P09). The 22 other vendors with CPNI, PII, or network access have not been reviewed, and the chatbot and CCaaS contracts lack CPNI, no-training, and 24-hour incident notice terms.
Unsupported components: TDM switches at CO-3, CO-5, and CO-7 (isolated, retirement 2028) and 2 SBCs reaching end of support 2026-12-31 (upgrade ordered).
Always-on DDoS scrubbing from two upstream providers protects internet edges, DNS, and hosted voice addresses.

Firewalls separate the internet, corporate, management, and cloud zones at CO-1, CO-4, and the cloud hub. Gaps: management VLAN reachable from corporate VLANs at POP-A and POP-B; SYS-10 shares the management path.

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Deny-by-default rules apply at the cloud hub and CO firewalls; POP firewalls still allow any-to-any between internal zones.
Data in transit is encrypted with TLS 1.2 or higher; CDR transfers from CO-1 to mediation use the site-to-cloud IPsec VPN.
Cloud keys are managed in the provider key service with company-managed keys for the production and backup accounts.
Approved cryptography is defined in STD-08 (TLS 1.2 or higher, AES-256 at rest).

provider_if_inherited: Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2); BSS vendor (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Data at rest is encrypted in the BSS, cloud storage, databases, backups, and endpoints. SYS-18 database encryption is unknown and under review.
Servers and endpoints are patched monthly. Network element patching is ad hoc; 2 edge routers missed the 30-day critical target (P07 SI-2).
EDR runs on all laptops, desktops, and servers with 24x7 MDR response.
The SIEM and MDR monitor IdP, cloud, endpoints, firewalls, and VPN. Network elements, CDR archive reads, SYS-15, and SYS-18 are not monitored (gap 7).
The security team tracks vendor advisories, CISA alerts, and the known exploited vulnerabilities catalog weekly and assigns network advisories to engineering.
Running images on core routers are verified against vendor hashes at upgrade. Access elements and SBCs are not verified.
Retention rules are in POL-04 (CPNI records at least 1 year, breach records at least 2 years). CDRs are kept 36 months online, longer than the 18 months the business needs.
A supply chain risk management plan is part of STD-03 (draft, due 2026-12-31).
Network equipment is bought from authorized channels. Used and refurbished equipment is bought from brokers without a Covered List check.
Supplier assessments cover 12 Tier 1 vendors; the remaining 22 vendors with CPNI, PII, or network access will be assessed by 2027-03-31.
